direction: Explore a narrow mix of absolute and normalized savings.
hypothesis: The normalized component may improve some near-tie decisions without giving up the useful far-customer preference.

operations.mechanism: Keep the adaptive angular incumbent and preserve depot ties. Use normalized savings only as a small secondary ranking signal when incumbent scores are close, or blend it with a dimensionally consistent local distance scale. Do not fully replace the primary absolute savings.

preserve: Keep the existing CVRP interface, read-only inputs, feasibility and deterministic evaluation. Preserve useful incumbent structure unless the mechanism calls for a deliberate pivot.
reasoning_summary: Both scale-normalized savings variants were valid. Candidate 2 scored 11.38412, better on instances 1–3 but worse on 0, 4 and 5. It normalized by radius sum plus savings and also added a distance tie break, so normalization alone is not isolated. Use the selected complete in-run Memory record as advisory context.
